# Quorum

A quorum sends one task to several models at once and merges what comes back. It
runs in this OpenCode instance, using the models the user already has, via the
`quorum` tool.

## When it is worth it

- A decision with consequences where you want genuinely independent takes
  (an architecture choice, a risky migration, a schema).
- A hard problem where one model may be confidently wrong.
- A second opinion on your own work — ask a different model to review it.
- Several independent attempts at one question, judged and merged
  (`vote`), when you want the answer to be reliable rather than merely plausible.

## When it is not

- Quick lookups, mechanical edits, or anything you can already answer.
- When the user asked for speed. A quorum costs one model call per member, plus
  one to merge — so four members is five calls.
- When the task needs tools and file access: prefer doing it yourself, or read the
  agent-mode note in `references/configuration.md` first, because agent workers
  edit the repository for real.

## Running one

Call the `quorum` tool with `action: "run"` (the default):

```
action: "run"
task:   "<the whole task, stated so it can stand alone>"
strategy: "vote" | "mixture" | "debate" | "divide" | "relay"
members: ["providerID/modelID", ...]     // omit to use the saved or automatic roster
copies: 1..8                             // >1 runs each member that many times
```

Write the `task` as a self-contained request — the members see only that text,
not this conversation. Then relay the merged answer, and say which models
produced it.

## Choosing a strategy

| Want | Use | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The best single answer | `mixture` | Everyone answers in parallel, one merges. The safe default. |
| A decision you can defend | `vote` | Independent answers, a judge picks and explains. |
| A contested judgement tested | `debate` | Models critique each other over rounds, then merge. |
| A big task split up | `divide` | A planner decomposes it, workers solve parts, results merge. |
| A draft made better | `relay` | Each model refines the previous one. |

Use `action: "models"` to see exact model references; guessing one wastes a run.

## A quorum of one model

`copies: 4` with `members` naming a single model runs four independent attempts
and is the self-consistency pattern — use it with `vote`. Each copy is given a
different framing on purpose, because a transient generation has no temperature
control; identical prompts to one model would come back nearly identical.

## Setting defaults up for the user

If the user wants a quorum *configured* rather than just run once, use
`action: "configure"`. It validates and saves, and tells you what it rejected:

```
action: "configure"
strategy: "vote"
members: ["opencode-go/gpt-6-luna"]
copies: 4
aggregator: "auto"      // or a model reference
```

Settings persist in `.opencode/quorum.json` and are used by every later run. The
full field list, and what each one costs, is in
`references/configuration.md`.

## Reading the result

`action: "status"` lists recent runs; `action: "cancel"` with a `runID` stops one.
A run's **warnings** are worth reading before you trust the answer: they name
models that failed, names that did not resolve, and whether the aggregator fell
back to a member's answer.

# Quorum for OpenCode [![CI](https://github.com/bradl3y21/opencode-quorum/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/bradl3y21/opencode-quorum/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) Run several OpenCode models on one task at the same time and merge what they produce into a single answer. Five ways to combine them, a `quorum` tool and a `/quorum` command, and an optional dashboard inside the desktop window. It uses the models you already have enabled in OpenCode. It has no API keys of its own. > **Renamed in 1.1.** This plugin was published as `opencode-plugin-swarm`. It > is now `opencode-quorum` — "swarm" in this ecosystem has come to mean a team > of agents building software, which is a different thing. A configuration file > written as `swarm.json` is still read, and the first write migrates it. > > **Unofficial.** Not affiliated with OpenCode or its maintainers. The dashboard > is an optional patch to the desktop app — read [Safety](#safety) before > installing it. Nothing else in this plugin modifies OpenCode. ## Requirements - OpenCode 2.x. Developed and tested against the desktop app **2.0.32**. - Node 20+ to run the installer and development harnesses (the plugin itself runs inside OpenCode). - The **dashboard is Windows only**, because it patches `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\@opencodedesktop\resources\app.asar`. The strategies, the `quorum` tool, `/quorum` and the TUI panel work on any platform. *The dashboard: pick a strategy, choose models, give it a task, and watch each step — then read or copy the merged answer.* ``` ┌─────────────┐ task → │ members │ → GLM-5.3 ─┐ │ (in parallel│ → Kimi K2.7 ├→ aggregator → one answer │ or in turn)│ → Hy3 ─┘ └─────────────┘ ``` ## What you get | Surface | Where it shows up | | --- | --- | | **Dashboard** | Optional, Windows only. A **Quorum** button in the title bar beside *Home* / *New session*, and a **Quorum** row above *Settings* on the home screen: pick models and strategy, type a task, watch every step live, read and copy the merged result. | | **`/quorum` command** | In any client's command menu. `/quorum ` runs a quorum; `/quorum debate ` forces a strategy; `/quorum status` lists recent runs. | | **`quorum` tool** | The agent can delegate to the quorum itself, and the tool card shows live per-model progress. | | **Timeline** | A run started from a session also mirrors its progress into that session, so you can watch it in the chat. | | **Terminal panel** | A TUI panel with the same features, for when you use the terminal client. | ## A quorum of one model `copies` runs each member several times, which is how you quorum a *single* model: ```json { "strategy": "vote", "members": ["opencode-go/gpt-6-luna"], "copies": 4 } ``` That runs four independent luna attempts and has luna judge the best — the self-consistency pattern, which genuinely improves reliability on judgement calls. Each copy is given a **different framing** (*first principles*, *risk-focused*, *edge cases*, *the sceptic*, …). That is deliberate: a transient generation takes only a prompt and a model, so there is no temperature or sampling control to vary, and four copies of the same prompt would come back much the same. Different lenses make the copies disagree in useful ways and give the aggregator something real to merge. `vote` is the natural strategy for it; `debate` is the odd one out, since a model would be critiquing its own copies. The panel exposes this as **Copies** next to Workers, and the `quorum` tool takes a `copies` argument. ## Choosing models Leave `members` empty and the quorum chooses for you: 1. it starts from the model **you are already using** for the project; 2. then takes one model from **each provider**, because different providers are where genuinely different answers come from; 3. it **steers around models that failed recently** (15 minutes) and **favours models that have answered recently** (1 hour); 4. it deprioritises giveaway tiers (`-free`, `-contributor`, `-preview`), and never picks the same model twice from two providers. That learning matters, because model metadata cannot tell you whether a model will actually answer: a free tier can refuse plugin calls outright, a provider can have a dead key, and a local provider may simply not be running. With the memory above, an automatic roster that started with 2 usable members out of 4 reached **all members succeeding by the third run**. You can always overrule it. Write members as `providerID/modelID`: ```json { "members": ["opencode-go/kimi-k2.7-code", "opencode-go/claude-opus-5-5"] } ``` A bare `modelID` is accepted too and resolved for you (`"kimi-k3"` → `opencode-go/kimi-k3`), and so is a wrong provider prefix. Anything that cannot be matched is reported in the run's notes rather than silently dropped. ## For agents This is set up so an agent in a session can use a quorum without being told how: - **A skill** at `.opencode/skills/quorum/SKILL.md`. OpenCode advertises it when a task looks like it deserves more than one model's opinion, and the agent loads it with the `skill` tool. It covers when a quorum is worth the cost, which strategy fits which question, and how to read a run's warnings. The field-level detail lives beside it in `references/configuration.md`, so it loads only when needed. - **A `configure` action** on the `quorum` tool, so an agent can set the defaults up rather than only run once. It validates: a bad strategy or an out-of-range `copies` is reported back and *not* written, rather than saved as a configuration the plugin cannot use. An agent can therefore be asked to "set up a quorum of luna 6 for reviews", and it will save the roster, strategy and copies itself. Editing `.opencode/quorum.json` by hand works too. ## Where it lives The panel is opened from OpenCode's own interface rather than from a floating button of its own: - **Title bar** — a Quorum button beside *Home* and *New session*, visible in every view. - **Sidebar** — a **Quorum** entry directly above *Settings* and *Help* on the home screen. - Both are **clones of the real controls** (the `New session` button and the `Settings` row), so they inherit OpenCode's exact sizing, spacing, hover, focus ring and icon treatment instead of imitating it, and both show as *selected* while the panel is open, using the app's own active-item styling. - The icon is OpenCode's own sprite glyph (`opencode-v2-icon-models`), not a custom drawing, so its weight matches the icons around it. - If neither anchor exists — a future layout change, or a narrow window where the sidebar collapses — a floating **Quorum** button appears instead, so the feature can never become unreachable. The drawer starts below the title bar, measured at runtime from the app's own `-webkit-app-region` drag areas, so nothing ever sits under the window controls (which are drawn above the page and would otherwise intercept a click). Editing configuration is **only possible through a real user interaction**: the panel ignores untrusted events, so a script or an automated client in the page cannot rewrite `quorum.json`. ## Strategies | Strategy | How the models work together | Good for | | --- | --- | --- | | `mixture` | Everyone answers in parallel; one model merges the results. | General questions, hard problems, "give me the best answer". | | `debate` | Models answer, then read each other and revise, for `rounds` rounds; a merge at the end. | Contested judgement calls, design decisions, catching errors. | | `divide` | A planner splits the task into subtasks, workers solve them in parallel, results are merged. | Big tasks that decompose cleanly. | | `relay` | Each model improves the previous model's draft in turn. | Polishing a draft, iterative refinement. | | `vote` | Models answer independently; a judge picks the strongest and explains why. | Decisions where you want a defensible pick. | ## Install The plugin is two independent parts, and you can take either: 1. **The server-side plugin** — the five strategies, the `quorum` tool, `/quorum` and the TUI panel. No app changes, no restart. 2. **The dashboard** — optional, Windows only, and the only part that patches the desktop app. ### 1. The server-side plugin Copy the `quorum` folder into your workspace's `.opencode/plugins/`, and the skill into `.opencode/skills/`: ```sh # from a clone of this repository git clone https://github.com/bradl3y21/opencode-quorum.git "/.opencode/plugins/quorum" mkdir -p "/.opencode/skills" cp -r "/.opencode/plugins/quorum/skills/quorum" "/.opencode/skills/quorum" ``` No dependencies to install — the plugin uses the runtime OpenCode provides. Restart OpenCode (or reload plugins). That is all: settings come from defaults until you create `.opencode/quorum.json` — start from `quorum.example.json`. If another plugin already registers a tool called `quorum` — for example the unrelated npm package `opencode-quorum` — disable one of them; two tools cannot share a name. This package is `opencode-quorum`. ### 2. The dashboard (optional, Windows) The desktop app has no plugin UI of its own, so the dashboard is a patch to `app.asar`. It is reversible and it verifies itself, but it is still a patch: ```sh cd .opencode/plugins/quorum/desktop node selftest.mjs # proves the archive writer is lossless node install.mjs # backs up app.asar, then adds the panel ``` The awkward catch: you drive this plugin *from* OpenCode, so you cannot quit the app and then ask for the install. Use the watcher — it breaks the deadlock by waiting for the gap: ```sh node install-when-free.mjs # leave it running, then quit OpenCode whenever ``` It refuses to act unless no `OpenCode.exe` is running **and** the archive is actually writable (so a slow app start cannot be patched mid-boot), runs the self-test first, and logs every step to `~/.local/share/opencode/log/quorum-install.log`. (The watcher is Windows-only; elsewhere, quit the app and run `install.mjs` directly.) After it finishes, just start OpenCode — the panel is already there. To confirm the result at any time: ```sh node verify.mjs # compares the patched archive to the backup ``` `install.mjs` copies `resources/app.asar` to `app.asar.quorum-backup` before its first write, and `node install.mjs --uninstall` restores that copy byte for byte. `node install.mjs --dry-run` shows exactly what would change without writing. It patches by **appending**: every existing file in the archive keeps its exact offset, size and bytes, and the panel plus the patched `index.html` are written after the existing data. Nothing is moved or re-packed. (An earlier version re-packed the archive and recomputed every offset; that broke an app update, because an archive's recorded boundaries are not always a perfect tiling.) One consequence worth knowing: the archive grows by roughly the size of the panel on each install, so `--uninstall` followed by a fresh `install.mjs` is the way to reclaim the space. It verifies afterwards that no existing entry moved, and `installer-test.mjs` proves the whole thing on copies, including a deliberately malformed archive. If you would rather not touch the app at all, or you want to iterate on the panel without restarting OpenCode, run the harness instead — it serves the real panel against the running server: ```sh cd .opencode/plugins/quorum/desktop && node harness.mjs # then open http://127.0.0.1:8799/ ``` ## Safety What the dashboard patch does: - adds one file, `/out/renderer/quorum-panel.js`, and replaces `index.html` with an identical copy carrying two extra `

# Quorum configuration

Settings live in `.opencode/quorum.json` (project) or `~/.config/opencode/quorum.json`
(global). The project file wins. The plugin re-reads it immediately, so a change
applies to the next run without restarting anything.

Prefer `action: "configure"` on the `quorum` tool: it validates values and tells
you what it rejected. Hand-editing this file works too, and `copies: …` is the
kind of setting a user may prefer to keep.

## What each setting costs

A `mixture` or `vote` run makes one model call per member, plus one to merge or
judge. `copies` multiplies the member count; `debate` multiplies it again by
`rounds`. So:

| Members | Copies | Rounds | Model calls (plus one) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | 1 | — | 5 |
| 1 | 4 | — | 5 |
| 3 | 1 | 2 | 7 (debate) |

Turn `autoMembers` down, or pin cheaper `members`, when a run needs to be cheap.

## Fields

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch. |
| `strategy` | `"mixture"` | `mixture`, `debate`, `divide`, `relay`, `vote`. |
| `members` | `[]` | Models as `"providerID/modelID"`. A bare `modelID` resolves too. Repeats are kept — naming one model four times runs it four times. Empty means automatic. |
| `copies` | `1` | Run each member this many times (1–8). Above 1, a quorum of the same model, each copy differently framed. |
| `aggregator` | first member | Model that merges the members' work. `auto` restores the default. |
| `planner` | first member | Model that splits the task, for `divide`. |
| `judge` | first member | Model that picks the winner, for `vote`. |
| `workerMode` | `"text"` | `text` or `agent`. See below. |
| `rounds` | `2` | Debate rounds, including the opening one. |
| `concurrency` | `4` | How many workers run at once. |
| `autoMembers` | `4` | How many models automatic selection picks. |
| `timeoutMs` | `180000` | Per-worker timeout for **text** workers. Text workers are single model calls, so two minutes is already generous. |
| `agentTimeoutMs` | `900000` | Per-worker timeout for **agent** workers. Agent workers are full sessions that read files, run commands and edit code, so they legitimately take many minutes — a shorter limit marks finished work as timed out. |
| `maxOutputChars` | `6000` | Truncate each answer before it reaches the aggregator — this is a real cost control, since every answer is pasted into the merge prompt. |
| `keepWorkerSessions` | `true` | Keep agent-mode worker sessions so they can be inspected. |
| `streamToSession` | `true` | Mirror progress into the session that started the run. |
| `tool` | `true` | Register the `quorum` tool. **Needs a reload.** |
| `command` | `true` | Register the `/quorum` command. **Needs a reload.** |
| `debugLog` | `true` | Append activity to `~/.local/share/opencode/log/quorum.log`. |

Environment variables mirror these: `OPENCODE_QUORUM_STRATEGY`, `_MEMBERS`
(comma separated), `_COPIES`, `_AGGREGATOR`, `_WORKER_MODE`, `_ROUNDS`,
`_CONCURRENCY`, `_AUTO_MEMBERS`, `_TIMEOUT_MS`, `_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS`,
`_MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS`, `_TOOL`, `_COMMAND`, `_DEBUG_LOG`.

## Worker modes

`text` (the default) is a plain model call: fast, cheap, no tools.

`agent` gives each model its own OpenCode session, so it can read files, run
commands and **edit the repository**. Before choosing it:

- every member works on the same checkout, so two models editing one file will
  conflict. For anything destructive, use a separate worktree or keep `text`.
- worker sessions are named `quorum · <role> · <model>` and nested under the
  session that started the run; `keepWorkerSessions: false` removes them once
  their answer is harvested.
- agent runs are far slower and more expensive than text runs.
- `agentTimeoutMs` (default 15 minutes) is separate from the text `timeoutMs`, and
  a timeout does not discard the work: whatever the session had produced is
  harvested and the step is kept, with a warning. Planning, judging and merging
  always run as text calls, in either mode — they never need tools.

## Choosing models

With `members` empty the quorum picks for you: it starts from the model the user is
already running, adds one model per provider, skips models that failed recently
(15 minutes) and favours models that answered recently (an hour). It deprioritises
giveaway tiers (`-free`, `-contributor`, `-preview`), which in practice are the
ones that refuse requests from a plugin.

That learning matters: model metadata cannot tell you whether a model will
actually answer. Ran against one workspace, an automatic roster went from two
usable members out of four on its first run to all members succeeding by the
third.
